$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §2 and docs/04-ARCHITECTURE.md §3. The canonical form of this object, under c14n v1, is what profile_sha256 hashes; the example below is the real v0 profile and its real digest, emitted by crates/ethos-parser-core and pinned in its tests.
title: Engine profile (DRAFT)
description: Every knob that can change output. Anything that can change a byte of output belongs here or is a bug. Host-varying data (paths, timings, thread counts, machine identity) is deliberately absent: including it would make every machine produce a different fingerprint for identical work.

parser_version.description: The engine build this profile describes. A new build is a new profile by design.

backend.description: Object/xref backend identity, so adopting or upgrading it is fingerprint-visible.

classify_sample_pages.description: How many pages classification samples before it stops. Default 8. Its boundedness is the point: cost must not scale with total page count.

reading_order_rule.description: Version id of the reading-order rule in force. Versioned because the rule is part of identity. `gutter-columns-v2` (D4-S2) is the same cut as `gutter-columns-v1` (v1-S5) — same constants, same order — and additionally reports the regions it made, as `region` on each text run; the id moved because the artifact gained a field, not because the sequence changed. `single-column-v1` means content-stream order with no reordering. `gutter-columns-v1` took a new id rather than bumping `single-column-v1`, because those two read different evidence and can list the same runs in a different sequence.

cmap_data_version.description: Identity of the vendored character-decoding data. Names what is actually vendored rather than what was planned: at M3 that is the PDF 32000-1 Annex D encoding tables, not the Adobe predefined CJK CMaps, whose absence is a declared limitation.

font_metrics_data_version.description: Identity of the vendored FONT METRIC data, distinct from cmap_data_version: that one names the tables turning a code into a character, this one the tables turning a character into an advance and a face into an ink envelope. At decision #22 that is Adobe's Core-14 AFMs in vendor/afm/, under APAFML. A standard-14 font the document names with no /Widths gains a measured ink box from them, so a run before and after this string existed produced different geometry and is correctly non-comparable.

xref_repair.description: Whether the one bounded cross-reference repair runs (v0.1). On the profile because it decides which documents produce an artifact at all.

verifier.description: Which verifier this run is bound to (v0.1). `not_pinned` is a declared state, not a missing field: the engine does not verify, it invokes a verifier, and a run that consulted none says so.

form_annotation_rule.description: Version id of the forms-and-annotations rule in force (v1-S4). Decides which form-field and annotation nodes exist: which flag bits are named, how a fully-qualified field name is built, and the fact that a widget's rendering is never read as page text. Named for what it does rather than the structure it reads, because ethos-parser-core carries no format concept.

struct_tree_rule.description: Version id of the structure-tree rule in force (v1-S3). Decides which runs come out carrying a role path: the recognised structure types, the /RoleMap handling, the /K depth bound, and the fact that the (page, mcid) join is exact equality rather than anything looser.

table_detection.description: The table-detection rules in force. An object rather than a string since v1-S2, three fields since v1-S8 and four since v2-S24: with several rules running, a single id could not say whether a run looked for a kind of table and found none or never looked, and those are different documents to a consumer. Every table on the wire also names the rule that produced it.

ruled.description: Version id of the rule that reconstructs grids from rectangles the document painted. `ruled-rects-v3`. A rectangle spanning the whole lattice is the table’s border, so it is neither emitted as a cell nor accepted as evidence that a face was drawn. Since v2-S20 a grid whose own structural cross-check rejects it — a slot two rectangles both claim — is refused rather than emitted, and the refusal is declared with its page and fault counts.

unruled.description: Version id of the rule that infers grids from text alignment. `unruled-align-v1`. A table it produced was inferred by this engine, not drawn by the author — which is why the ids are separate.

stroke_ruled.description: Version id of the rule that reconstructs grids from stroked ruling lines (v1-S8). `stroke-ruled-v1`. A two-point stroked segment is the author saying `this edge is here`, which is evidence they left rather than an inference this engine made — so it ranks with the ruled rule and above the alignment one. Rows are the regions between rules, so a grid whose top edge was never drawn comes back one row short rather than completed.

tagged.description: Version id of the rule that emits a table for each `/Table` the structure tree declares that no geometric detector matched (v2-S24). `tagged-tables-v1`. This one reads the document's own tags rather than ink, so its table is `Extracted` — the document's own statement — rather than `Computed`, and it carries no geometry: the tree names no coordinate, so the box is absent (`not_reported_by_structure_tree`) and none is invented. Its locator cross-check is not-applicable, and it is omitted from any `ethos.grounding.v1` projection.

markdown_rule.description: Version id of the Markdown projection rule in force (v1.1-S1, moved at S2 and again at S3). Decides what `ethos.markdown.v1` contains: which nodes project, whether a table becomes a GFM grid or a run of paragraphs, whether a tagged list becomes list items, whether a heading comes from the structure tree or an EPUB's own `<h1>`-`<h6>`, whether a word the page broke across a line is closed up in the export, and the whitespace rule a source segment's bytes are normalized under. A profile predating v1.1-S1 carries no such key and is REFUSED rather than defaulted — a field defaulted in is a claim the run never made.

html_rule.description: Version id of the HTML projection rule in force (v1.1-S4). Decides what `ethos.html.v1` contains. SEPARATE from `markdown_rule` and it moves independently: the two projections say different things about the same table, because GFM has no `rowspan` and `<td rowspan>` does, so one id covering both would make every artifact non-comparable each time either moved. A profile predating v1.1-S4 carries no such key and is REFUSED rather than defaulted — a field defaulted in is a claim the run never made.

observation_rule.description: Version id of the image and text-finding rule in force (v1-S6). Decides which `Do` calls become image nodes, how a painted rectangle is derived from the page's own matrix, and what counts as invisible or off-page text.

text_code_rule.description: Version id of the character-code rule in force (v1-S6.1). Decides how a string operand is divided into character codes: a simple font is one byte per code (PDF 32000-1 9.6), a composite font's width belongs to the CMap its /Encoding names (9.7.5). Distinct from cmap_data_version, which names the vendored encoding TABLES — this names how a string is divided before any table is consulted.

capabilities.title: What this profile claims it can do
capabilities.description: L1's achievement condition names capability declarations explicitly, so an artifact without them has not reached 'extracted' regardless of how good its text is. The first three mirror ethos.grounding.v1's required capabilities object exactly.
capabilities.$comment: Two rules bind this object in both directions, and both are enforced by tests rather than by review. No `true` without a named proof test: crates/ethos-parser-pdf/tests/capabilities.rs maps each true field to a test function and fails the build when the named test does not exist. No `false` without a declared limitation: Capabilities::declared_limitations() derives one per false field, exhaustively, so a consumer never infers a gap from silence.

char_offsets.$comment: FALSE in v0, and it was true in the M1 sketch. v0 emits runs with native locators and no element/span hierarchy, so there is nothing for an offset to index into. It flips at M5 with DocumentRepresentation v0 — and with a test. Narrowing a declaration when the evidence does not support it is the mechanism working, not a regression.

tables.$comment: true since v1-S1 (ruled), widened at v1-S2 (unruled)

measured_ink_boxes.$comment: true in v0 — proof: measured_ink_boxes_are_measured_and_absence_stays_typed, which asserts both halves (a measured box exists, and unusable metrics still yield typed absence rather than a fallback)

multi_column_reading_order.$comment: true since v1-S5 — proof: multi_column_order_is_read_and_single_column_is_left_alone. Where the rule finds no gutter it reorders nothing, and reading-order-geometric-only declares what it still cannot see. A profile setting this false declares multi-column-reading-order instead and must also name single-column-v1

structural_locators.$comment: FALSE in v0. An mcid IS captured where a page's content stream supplies one via BDC, and never invented where it does not — but the tagged-structure tree is not read, so there is no role path and an absent mcid is not evidence the document is untagged. Claiming the capability on the strength of the partial half would promise an address consumers could not rely on.

images.$comment: true since v1-S6 — proof: an_image_is_a_node_with_a_placement_and_a_digest. Claims only that this profile LOOKS: a page painting none yields no image nodes. Images inside form XObjects are not seen and inline images are counted rather than emitted, both separately declared — and since 0.45.0 the form XObjects a document actually drew are counted too, on `form-xobjects-not-descended`, outside this flag: what that count declares is text this reader did not read rather than a picture it declined to emit. Carries no description, caption or alt text — that would be OCR or a model's opinion, and neither is evidence (checklist O20).

markdown.description: A Markdown projection is emitted, always with its Anchor Map (v1.1-S1). What it claims is narrow: THIS PROFILE CAN PROJECT the representation into Markdown that stays citable. It does not claim the Markdown is pretty or complete. False obliges `markdown-not-projected`, which is a position rather than a gap — checklist O8 records that rule 8 prefers no projection at all.

page_screenshots.$comment: false at v1-S6, by decision rather than omission. Rendering needs a PDF renderer; PDFium is admitted only caller-provided under an explicit ADR, no AGPL renderer clears the licence allowlist, and shelling out to a converter would put an unpinned binary between the document and the artifact. Partnered by `page-raster-not-emitted`, with `raster_dpi` recording the not-emitted state so a renderer arriving later moves profile_sha256.

html.description: An HTML projection is emitted, always with its Anchor Map (v1.1-S4). Separate from `markdown` because the two artifacts say different things about the same document, and a consumer choosing between them is choosing which erasures it can afford.

page_budget.title: How many pages a run may process before it stops
page_budget.$comment: A DECLARED STATE, not an absent field: {"mode":"unlimited"} says the budget was considered and found unbounded, where an omitted optional would leave a reader unable to tell 'unbounded' from 'this build has no such knob' — and would deserialize to a default that silently re-hashes as though it had been there. A page count is the knob because it is the bound that actually governs peak cost in a page-at-a-time reader. Setting it changes profile_sha256, so a budgeted run is correctly non-comparable with an unbudgeted one.

oneOf.description: No page bound. The v0 default.

pages.$comment: Zero is legal and means 'process none'. It is the only budget that can bite on a one-page document, which is what failure/memory-limit-simulated needs: that fixture is byte-identical to synthetic/simple-text, so its name means the limit is simulated BY CONFIGURATION, not that the PDF is large.

oneOf.description: Process at most this many pages; the rest are quarantined and declared, and the run's terminal state is partial.

raster_dpi.description: The resolution page rasters are emitted at, or a declared reason there are none (v1-S6). A DECLARED STATE rather than an absent field, exactly as page_budget is: {"mode":"not_emitted"} says this profile considered rasters and emits none, where an omitted key would leave a reader unable to tell that from a build with no such knob at all — and would let a future renderer arrive without moving profile_sha256.
raster_dpi.$comment: Adjacently tagged with a `dpi` content key in Rust, so a future {"mode":"dpi","dpi":300} is additive. Internally tagged would silently drop an unknown sibling key and re-hash as though it had never been there.
